### NHI Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results


November 9, 2026


MURFREESBORO, Tenn.


, Nov. 9, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- National Health Investors, Inc. (NYSE: NHI) announced today its results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


**CEO Comments**


"SHOP and private-pay senior housing remain central to our long-term growth strategy, and we have invested in our executive management team to strengthen operating execution and improve portfolio performance," said Eric Mendelsohn, NHI's President and CEO. "Our strengthened team has developed a focused plan to address underperformance and position the portfolio for sustainable NOI growth consistent with our underwriting standards."


"We have closed more than $395 million in investments year-to-date and expect to complete significant additional investments before year-end, with ample capital available to fund our current pipeline. This activity reflects our continued confidence in private-pay senior housing and our ability to source attractive opportunities. Our focus remains on disciplined capital allocation and stronger operating execution to translate that growth into long-term value for stockholders," concluded Mr. Mendelsohn.


**Third Quarter Highlights**


- Net income attributable to common stockholders per diluted share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $11.47 per share compared to $0.69 per share for the same period in the prior year. Net income attributable to common stockholders per diluted share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $13.52 per share compared to $2.22 per share for the same period in the prior year. During the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized a gain of $541.6 million on the sale of the National Healthcare Corporation ("NHC") leased portfolio completed on July 1, 2026 and recognized $9.9 million of impairment to a real estate property from the Real Estate Investments segment which was reclassified to assets held for sale in the current quarter. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company sold a total of 42 real estate properties from the Real Estate Investments segment for aggregate net proceeds of $672.1 million and recognized a total gain on dispositions of real estate properties of $567.5 million.
- National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts ("NAREIT") Funds from Operations ("FFO") per diluted share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 increased 2.8% to $1.12 per share compared to $1.09 per share for the same period in the prior year. NAREIT FFO per diluted share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased 3.5% to $3.54 per share compared to $3.42 per share for the same period in the prior year. During the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, resident fees and services, less senior housing operating expenses, increased $6.6 million and $19.6 million, respectively, due to the acquisition of 20 properties in the SHOP segment. During each of the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2025, NAREIT FFO included a $10.8 million and $11.0 million, respectively in net reduction in rental income for the lease terminations associated with the seven properties transitioned to the SHOP segment in August 2025.
- Normalized FFO per diluted share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 decreased 15.2% to $1.12 per share compared to $1.32 per share for the same period in the prior year. Normalized FFO per diluted share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 decreased 4.1% to $3.54 per share compared to $3.69 per share for the same period in the prior year. Normalized FFO for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026 included $1.1 million of transaction costs related to acquisitions the Company stopped pursuing. Normalized FFO for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 included $1.0 million of deferred income tax expense. Normalized FFO for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2025 included a $3.9 million reduction in cash rental income related to the lease termination of the transitioned properties, and Normalized FFO for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 included a $3.4 million reduction in credit loss reserves.
- Normalized Funds Available for Distribution (“FAD”) for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 decreased $5.1 million to $57.1 million compared to $62.2 million for the same period in the prior year. Normalized FAD for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased $7.0 million to $181.2 million compared to $174.2 million for the same period in the prior year. During the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, resident fees and services, less senior housing operating expenses, increased $5.5 million and $13.2 million, respectively, from the acquisition of 20 properties since the fourth quarter of 2025. Cash rental income decreased $11.8 million and $11.5 million, respectively, due to the disposition of 42 properties in the Real Estate Investments segment, which included the 35 properties comprising the NHC portfolio.


**Third Quarter Financial Results**


Results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in the prior year were impacted by the following:


- Rental income decreased $1.5 million, or 2.5%, primarily due to an $11.8 million decrease in cash rental income from 42 dispositions since July 1, 2025. In addition, the Company had a $6.0 million decrease in cash rental income related to the seven properties transitioned to the SHOP segment in August 2025. These decreases were partially offset by a $2.8 million increase in cash rental income from five acquisitions since July 1, 2025 and the write-off of $12.1 million of straight-line rents receivable on the seven properties transitioned to the SHOP segment. Additionally, the rental income decrease was offset by $2.2 million of rent escalators.
- Resident fees and services, less senior housing operating expenses, increased $6.6 million, primarily due to a $5.5 million increase from the acquisition of 20 properties in the SHOP segment since the beginning of the fourth quarter of 2025 and a $0.5 million increase from the seven transitioned properties discussed above.


- On a same store ("Same Store") basis, resident fees and services, less senior housing operating expenses, increased $0.6 million.


- Interest income from mortgage and other notes receivable decreased $1.3 million, or 20.6%, primarily due to a net reduction in the principal amounts of mortgage and other notes receivable outstanding in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the prior year period.
- Depreciation and amortization increased $5.5 million, or 27.4%, primarily due to a $6.2 million increase from properties acquired after July 1, 2025, partially offset by a $1.3 million decrease related to properties sold after July 1, 2025 and one property that was classified as assets held for sale as of September 30, 2026.
- Interest expense decreased $1.2 million, or 9.0%, which primarily consisted of a $3.4 million decrease from the repayments of term loans in 2025, a $2.4 million decrease attributable to the Credit Facility and a $4.5 million increase due to the 2033 Senior Notes issued in September 2025.
- Legal expense of $1.1 million in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 consisted primarily of the costs incurred for a large transaction in the SHOP segment which the Company is no longer pursuing.
- General and administrative expenses increased $1.7 million, or 26.8%, in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 primarily due to a $1.0 million increase in compensation costs, mostly related to headcount and share-based compensation, and a $0.5 million increase in professional fees.
- Loan and realty losses, net, of $9.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 primarily included $9.9 million of impairment recognized on a property in the Real Estate Investments segment which the Company sold in November 2026. Loan and realty gains, net, of $2.0 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 primarily included a reduction of credit loss reserves on notes receivable that were repaid in the prior year period.
- Gains on dispositions of real estate properties of $542.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 primarily related to the gain recognized on the sale of the NHC portfolio.
- Other non-operating income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 primarily consisted of interest earned on the proceeds from the sale of the NHC portfolio.


**Portfolio Activity**


- In July 2026, the Company sold its portfolio of 35 properties leased to NHC/OP, L.P., a wholly-owned subsidiary of NHC, and certain of its affiliates. The Company recognized $560.0 million in cash consideration, $5.3 million of closing costs and a $541.6 million gain on the sale. The NHC portfolio was included in the Real Estate Investments segment and consisted of 32 SNFs and three ILFs that were initially acquired by the Company in 1991.
- In July 2026, the Company completed the sale of two skilled nursing facilities located in Texas that were included in the Real Estate Investments segment. The Company recognized $18.9 million in cash consideration, $0.1 million of closing costs and a $1.5 million gain on the sale.
- In October 2026, the Company acquired a portfolio of six senior housing communities located in Kentucky, Michigan and Tennessee that have been included in the SHOP segment. The total purchase price was $107.7 million, including $1.2 million of closing costs. The portfolio, which consists of five ALFs and one ILF with a combined total of 443 units, is being managed by Allegro Living Management.
- In October 2026, the Company purchased an assisted living facility located in Michigan from Bickford for $16.8 million that has been included in the Real Estate Investments segment. In connection with the purchase, Bickford repaid its $14.7 million construction loan which was secured by this property. The property is being leased back to Bickford pursuant to an existing master lease agreement that has an annual lease rate of 8.70% and expires in May 2033.
- In October 2026, the Company purchased an inpatient rehabilitation hospital from The Sanders Trust, LLC for $34.6 million. The property is located in Florida and has been included in the Real Estate Investments segment. In connection with the purchase, The Sanders Trust, LLC repaid its $27.6 million construction loan which was secured by this property. The Company assumed the existing lease on the property with ClearSky Lake City which has an annual lease rate of 8.25% and expires in October 2046.
- *In November 2026, the Company completed the sale of an assisted living facility located in Illinois for $3.3 million in cash consideration. During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized $9.9 million of impairment related to this property. This property was included in the Real Estate Investments segment and classified as assets held for sale as of September 30, 2026.*


**Recent Pipeline Developments**


- The Company currently has approximately $285.3 million of investment opportunities under signed Letters of Intent ("LOI") primarily in the SHOP segment with an expected average initial NOI yield of approximately 6.5%.
- In addition to the signed LOIs, the Company is currently evaluating a pipeline of approximately $400 million of investments which include SHOP, sale-leasebacks and loans with purchase options primarily for senior housing properties. The pipeline excludes portfolio deals.


**Balance Sheet and Liquidity**


As of September 30, 2026, the Company had $1.0 billion of consolidated net debt, including $203.0 million outstanding on its $700.0 million revolving credit facility. The Company had $46.6 million of cash and cash equivalents, $231.7 million of restricted cash and $108.3 million of deposits for future acquisitions.


The Company continues to maintain a strong financial profile with a consolidated net debt to annualized adjusted EBITDA ratio of 3.6x, which is currently well within the Company's target range of 3.5x to 4.5x. The Company is in compliance with all debt covenants as of September 30, 2026 and has investment grade credit ratings from Moody's, S&P Global and Fitch Ratings.


**ATM Equity Program**


Concurrently with the renewal of its shelf registration statement in March 2026, the Company entered into a new equity distribution agreement for the sale of up to $500.0 million in common stock under its ATM equity program. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had $500.0 million available under its ATM equity program.


**Dividend**


On November 6, 2026, the Company's board of directors declared a $0.94 per share dividend payable on January 29, 2027 to common stockholders of record as of December 31, 2026.

**About National Health Investors, Inc.**


National Health Investors, Inc. (NYSE: NHI), established in 1991 as a Maryland corporation, is a self-managed real estate investment trust ("REIT"). The Company owns, leases, operates and finances the development of high-quality real estate properties throughout the United States, focusing on senior housing communities and medical facilities. The Company operates through two reportable segments, Real Estate Investments and SHOP. The Company's real estate property investments include independent living facilities, assisted living facilities, entrance fee communities, senior living campuses, skilled nursing facilities and hospitals. For more information, visit[www.nhireit.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4817721-1&h=4240448460&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nhireit.com%2F&a=www.nhireit.com) .

**Notes to the Reconciliations of FFO, Normalized FFO, Normalized FAD, NOI and Same Store**


The supplemental performance measures described below may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other REITs. Consequently, funds from operations ("FFO"), Normalized FFO, Normalized FAD, NOI and Same Store, as presented herein, may not provide a meaningful measure of the Company's performance as compared to that of other REITs. Since other REITs may not use a similar definition of these performance measures, caution should be exercised when comparing FFO, Normalized FFO, Normalized FAD, NOI and Same Store, as presented herein, to that of other REITs. These performance measures do not represent cash generated from operating activities in accordance with GAAP as they exclude the changes in operating assets and liabilities, and therefore should not be considered an alternative to net income as an indication of performance or as an alternative to net cash flows from operating activities, as determined in accordance with GAAP as a measure of liquidity, and are not necessarily indicative of cash available to fund cash needs. We calculate basic and diluted weighted average shares outstanding on a similar basis to GAAP when calculating our non-GAAP financial measures on a per share basis.


*Funds From Operations - FFO*


FFO and Normalized FFO are important supplemental performance measures for REITs. These performance measures are useful in that the historical cost accounting convention under GAAP requires real estate assets, other than land, to be depreciated over their estimated useful lives implying that the realizable values of real estate assets diminish predictably over time. Since real estate asset values typically rise and fall with market conditions, presentations of operating results of REITs using the historical cost accounting convention could be considered less informative to investors and should be supplemented with a measure such as FFO. FFO was designed by the REIT industry as a supplemental performance measure to address this issue.


The Company defines FFO, or NAREIT FFO, as net income attributable to common stockholders excluding gains on dispositions of real estate properties, impairments of real estate properties and real estate depreciation and amortization expense. These exclusions are adjusted to remove the impact of amounts that are attributable to noncontrolling interests and holders of participating securities. The Company's computation of FFO may not be comparable to FFO reported by other REITs that do not define the term in accordance with the current NAREIT definition or have a different interpretation of the current NAREIT definition from that of the Company, and therefore caution should be exercised when comparing the Company's FFO to that of other REITs.


Normalized FFO excludes from FFO certain items which, due to their infrequent or unpredictable nature, may create some difficulty in comparing FFO for the current periods to similar prior periods. These adjustments may include, but are not limited to, impairments of non-real estate assets, gains or losses on non-real estate assets and liabilities and recoveries of previous write-downs on mortgage and other notes receivable.


*Funds Available for Distribution - FAD*


Normalized FAD is also an important supplemental performance measure for REITs. It is a useful measure of liquidity and serves as an indicator of the Company's ability to distribute dividends to its stockholders each period. GAAP requires a lessor to recognize contractual lease payments as income on a straight-line basis over the expected term of the lease. This straight-line rent adjustment has the effect of reporting rental income that is significantly more or less than the contractual cash flows received pursuant to the terms of the lease agreements. GAAP also requires any discount or premium related to indebtedness and debt issuance costs to be amortized as non-cash adjustments to earnings. Normalized FAD includes adjustments for these types of non-cash items of a recurring nature typical to REITs and is further adjusted to reflect the cash outflows for recurring capital expenditures. Certain other costs that fluctuate that are not related to the recurring business are also excluded from Normalized FAD.


The Company defines Normalized FAD as Normalized FFO excluding straight-line rent revenue adjustments, amortization of lease incentives, non-real estate depreciation and amortization expense, amortization of debt issuance costs and discounts and certain transaction costs. The Company also adjusts Normalized FAD for the net change in its credit loss reserves, share-based compensation expense, SHOP capital expenditures, deferred income tax expense, as well as certain non-cash items related to the Company's equity method investment, such as straight-line lease expense and amortization of purchase accounting adjustments. The Company removes the impact of the above adjustments that are attributable to noncontrolling interests and holders of participating securities. Normalized FAD for each of the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 included adjustments for transaction costs which related to transactions in the SHOP segment that the Company stopped pursuing during these periods.


*NOI*


NOI is a non-GAAP supplemental financial measure used to evaluate the operating performance of real estate assets. The Company defines NOI as total revenues, less tenant reimbursements of property operating expenses and senior housing operating expenses. The Company believes NOI provides relevant and useful information to investors as it measures the operating performance of real estate assets at the property level on an unleveraged basis. The Company also uses NOI in making decisions about resource allocations to its operating segments.


*Same Store*


The Company defines Same Store as real estate properties owned, consolidated and operational for the full period in both comparative periods and that are not otherwise excluded; provided, however, that the Company may include selected properties that otherwise meet the Same Store criteria if they are included in substantially all of, but not a full, period for one or both of the comparative periods, and in management's judgment such inclusion provides a more meaningful presentation of the Company's segment performance.


Newly acquired properties, recently developed or redeveloped properties and properties undergoing an operator transition will be included in Same Store after five full quarters from the date of acquisition, transition or being placed into service. SHOP properties and properties with triple-net leases that have undergone operator or business model transitions will be included in Same Store once operating under consistent operating structures for the full period in both periods presented.


Properties are excluded from Same Store if they are: (i) sold, classified as assets held for sale or properties whose operations were classified as discontinued operations in accordance with GAAP; (ii) impacted by significant disruptive events such as flood or fire; (iii) those properties that are currently undergoing a significant disruptive redevelopment; or (iv) those properties that are scheduled to undergo operator or business model transitions, or have transitioned operators or business models after the start of the prior comparison period.
